description: I'm an engineering student interested in space science, Python, AI/ML, and satellite data analysis. I have experience working with scientific datasets and developing machine-learning models. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I want to explore SPHEREx mission data and build an interactive, user-friendly tool to visualize astronomical observations and changes over time.
summary:
StellarCipher is an interactive web-based tool developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

The project aims to make SPHEREx astronomical observations more accessible and easier to explore. It provides a platform for examining real SPHEREx sky data and investigating astronomical images, helping users explore potential changes and objects of interest across observations.

Built using Python and Streamlit, StellarCipher offers an accessible interface for exploring astronomical data without requiring users to work directly with complex scientific data files. It serves as an exploratory tool for preliminary investigation and candidate identification, encouraging further analysis of interesting observations.

By connecting NASA's SPHEREx mission data with an accessible web application, StellarCipher aims to bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and public scientific exploration.
details:
StellarCipher is an interactive web-based astronomical exploration tool developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

The application is designed to help users explore SPHEREx infrared sky observations, compare images across different observation periods, and investigate regions that may contain interesting astronomical changes or candidate signals.

StellarCipher focuses on three key functions: Observe, Compare, and Investigate. The Observe feature allows users to explore infrared image exposures. Compare helps examine changes between different observation epochs, while Investigate supports the closer inspection and prioritization of candidate signals with their associated provenance.

The application is developed using Python and Streamlit, providing an accessible and interactive web interface without requiring users to work directly with complex scientific datasets or specialized software.

The main objective is to make astronomical data exploration more approachable, encourage public engagement with NASA's SPHEREx mission, and support preliminary investigation of changing objects and regions in the universe.
